title: arma 2: private military company
text: ### UPDATE. IMPORTANT EDIT: I'm downrating this one due to endless bugs that cripple the gameplay. When you spend 1 hour trying to figure out how to end a mission that has been haunted by a severe bug, it means you are not playing the game any more. I am seriously tired of how annoying this game is. Intriguing? Yes. Playable? Nah. So here I am, defending an airport. Except there is this guy leading the team who keeps setting waypoints some 798 m away from where action is... possibly following an enemy that the system respawned where it shouldn't have. Every AI is running around like an idiot trying to make sense of a map that is simply too big for the mission at end (in this mission, you use only 10% of the entire map for meaningful purposes. The rest is but a barren wasteland where occasional respawns make it impossible to complete the mission). But that's not all! So here I am. I climbed the ladder and I am facing a sniper. Yeah, a sniper wearing a headscarf. I look at him. He looks at me. Why isn't he shooting me? I mean, I'm even playing Veteran here, but this guy does not seem willing to end my life. He simply stares at me! That's nothing short of incredible. ...And why am I staring at him? Suprise: I ran out of bullets and have just realized this game has no control to hit him in the face. Man, I cannot even push you down the building, hoping the fall would kill you. It's a stall. Of course I can go back and fetch some ammo, but the sheer idea of facing this scripted thing that stares back at me and doesn't shoot... paired with my inability to fight back with my bare hands... I mean, not even COD touched the bottom of the barrel. PMC did! ### OLD REVIEW FOLLOWS ### ArmA 2: PMC builds on Operation Arrowhead, but from a different viewpoint -- i.e. that of private contractors who work in war zones. Some interesting things: - The plot is intriguing; - Scenarios are a pleasure for the eye; - Somewhat challenging; - It crashes way less than all the other arma games; - Easier controls. However, be warned that it is not your traditional ArmA 2 game, because it downgrades a lot of aspects that made ArmA 2 famous. I do not take an issue with that: it is a matter of choices, but just do expect something a bit more like COD and a bit less like ArmA. Some things to consider: - Differently form other ArmA games, here you spend most of your time on the field as a single individual. Most of this game takes away all the "troop management thing" that was typical of ArmA; - The world is not open-ended. Scenarios are broad and fully explorable, yet they contain very little beyond the mission's limited scope. I remember running around, searching houses... but, in the end, that's just a tour of the gaming world, but it does not add to its background and story; at best, you'll end up in a nicely designed empty shelled building; - Most mission and plots are mono-rail: you have to do A, B, C, and D in line to get to the end. It feels like a rollercoaster most of the time. Nothing against this, yet, again, this is not the open-ended world but rather a glorified version of the good old Call of Duty series. Just stay on track and do what you are told; - Some other reviewers noticed that sometimes realism is sacrificed to the sake of the storyline. I think the issue is a bit deeper than that: there is a mission in which you have to take down a series of vehicles one by one with an anti-materiel rifle. It is not that the mission isn't challenging per se... however, with some grain of salt you will keep asking yourself: don't the people on the vehicles communicate with each other? Do they keep standing there or following the same scripted path just for you to drop in and take a shot? Basically, at some stage this game will make you feel like the AI could have done better; - Game-breaking situations, in which a mission is extremely difficult if you play as the gunner, but it gets piece of cake if you set yourself on the driver's seat... - Longevity is not very good: the time you see next to my name (28 hrs) is what it takes for you to get to the mission before the last one, assuming you will go through some missions more than once to maximize your results. This means that the entire campaign is much shorter if you consider the actual game time required to finish the game. ...and so on. Final assessment: game is recommended if you want a different kind of experience with the ArmA engine. Possibly a more affordable and easy one... and if you are intrigued by Middle-Eastern scenarios. But that's about it.

text: Typical of the Arma games: you only get to see the games in their full glory ten years after being released due to affordable computer hardware lagging behind for miles. I don't get it ... why not make Arma 3 using the version of the engine used in Arma Gold (or 'Armed Assault'). At least we'd get a game everyone would be able to run and enjoy. Okay, the old engine could probably use some tweaking and optimization but it's not fundamentally different from the newer engine versions and yet my quad core CPU and medium rang graphics card still struggle to render a village environment in Arma 3 with viewing distance set to a meager 1.200m ... Imagine how terrific a viewing distance of 1.200m would be when flying an aircraft and trying to locate a ground target while also avoiding enemy AA ?! - That's right, it isn't ... In Arma Gold I can easily turn up the viewing distance to 5.000m, have medium/high detail settings and still have nice frame rates. To cut a long story short: this game runs like a charm and basically offers the same gameplay that Arma 2 and 3 have to offer. There are plenty of mods and addons to enrich the experience and for the price it's an absolute steal. Get it! Note: I'm using Windows 7 (64 bit)

title: audiosurf
text: Audiosurf converts any music in your pc in an obstacle course to be traversed with a variety of ships with distinct powers and gameplay styles. +The idea, while not outrageously original, is really cool and nicely executed. Literally whatever music you dump into the game will become a track with its difficulty based on the speed, complexity and flow of the song. It's really fun to play this game to one of your favorite songs, and even a barebone experience without any gameplay variations is nice. +3 tiers of difficulty and various different ships with equally different mechanics, that range from a simple, straightforward ride to enjoy the music and the track to score-busting abilities that greatly change the pace of the game in favor of a more proper "game" experience compared to the simpler, "experience"-style base ship. There's even the co-op ship! +Those obsessed with leaderboards will of course find a whole lot of them here. +It's cheap, it's small, it runs on a toaster and is perfect for short sessions too, while still having a hardcore appeal thanks to its more elaborate ships and higher difficulties. -It's a simple game with a simple concept and it does that and nothing more, so you'd better make sure it fits your style. -Visually the game looks... kind of nice, hypnotizing and trippy with its disco colors and feel, but it's quite basic on this side. Audiosurf 2, which is out by the way, has much more flair and options, if you want a more complete experience, but it's also significantly more expensive and has quite some useless fluff in it, so some people still favor this game over its sequel. -Not all tracks make for great... tracks (forgive me). Slow music (i.e. some jazz, ballads, romantic songs etc) will produce slow, boring circuits with nearly no difficulty. Beware of the opposite end of the spectrum, since songs with a high bpm can instead turn into extremely difficult tracks. Audiosurf is a classic example of a very simple game that, depending on your personal liking, can have as much longevity as is the music you can feed it. You can like this game because it is a good offer for record hunters, or because it's an entertaining way to interact with your music beyond just listening to it. If you think that's the case, the bunch of euros this game costs are surely worth it.
